newsitem.title: USA: MORTGAGE-BACKED MART DIGESTS GNMA, FNMA PREPAYS.
newsitem.headline: MORTGAGE-BACKED MART DIGESTS GNMA, FNMA PREPAYS.

text.p: Mortgage securities were firmer at midday as market players were busy digesting July Federal National Mortgage Association (FNMA) and Government National Mortgage Association (GNMA) prepayment data.
Discount coupon prices were 4/32 to 5/32 firmer, while premium coupons were up 1/32 to 2/32.
An increase in July prepayments was evident in both FNMA and GNMA pools, but FNMA mortgage loans saw more pronounced activity, according to market participants.

The heightened prepayment activity came as no surprise to market participants because of the decline in U.S. interest rates. Homeowners, more than ever, are viewed as savvy consumers ready to cut mortgage loan costs via a refinancing.
In July, participants said, FNMA loan pools with a 7.0 percent coupon came in 11.0 percent faster at 6.0 CPR (constant prepayment rate).
While coupons lower than 7.0 percent saw "fairly modest increases of about 3.0 percent to 8.0 percent," higher coupons saw more significant increases in prepayments.

According to market participants, 7.5 percent coupons were 19 percent faster at 6.4 CPR, while 8.0 percent coupons were 33 percent faster at 9.6 CPR. In the meantime, 8.5 percent coupons were 74 percent faster at 19.6 CPR and 9.0 percent coupons were 57 percent at 28.1 CPR, market participants said.
Seasonal patterns are said to be behind some of the heightened prepayment activity, but higher coupons were those most likely to be affected by lower rates.
One market player said that August prepayment reports likely would show continued refinancings because of the sharp decline in rates seen last Thursday.
GNMA speeds were faster as well, although the increases were not as large as those seen in FNMA loan pools, said participants.

Market players reported that newly issued GNMA 7.5 percent coupons were 38 percent faster at 5.3 CPR, while GNMA 8.0 percent coupons were 44 percent faster at 7.6 CPR. Also, GNMA 8.5 percent coupons were 3.0 percent faster at 14.7 CPR and newly issued 9.0 percent coupons were 5.0 percent faster at 23.3 CPR.

Continued increases in the weekly refinancing index survey compiled by the Mortgage Bankers Association of America were not viewed as surprising given the low rate cloud that has lingered in recent weeks, market observers agreed.
As reported, U.S. mortgage refinancing applications rose 15.7 percent in the week ended August 7 and represented 34 percent of the week's activity.
Investors, meanwhile, were seen closely watching the results of the final leg of the U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding auction. The Treasury sells $10 billion in 30-year bonds Thursday.

At midday, 30-year GNMA 7 1/2 percent bonds were up 3/32 at 101-12/32 for a bond equivalent yield of 7.32 percent. That yield was 107 basis points above the outstanding Treasury 10-year note, which was unchanged at 99-16/32 to yield 6.19 percent.
Among other 30-year 7 1/2-percent issues, FNMA and FHLMC bonds were up 3/32 at 101-12/32 and 101-18/32, respectively.
